composition_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-preserving composition revision.
INPUT 1 is the EDIT TARGET: Design 2 Ming-inspired King of Spades costume study. INPUT 2 is Design 1's completed King of Spades, a COMPOSITION reference ONLY. INPUT 3 is Design 2's approved black lotus back, the FLORAL VOCABULARY reference.
Create ONE revised Design 2 King of Spades card bringing input 1 toward input 2's finished composition. Preserve the recognizable Chinese man, both visible eyes looking slightly toward viewer's right, moustache and tapered beard, black Ming upward-folded-wing cap, yellow silk round-collar dragon robe, red inner collar, jade plaque belt, teal/madder cuffs, two opposing waist-up figures, small central turquoise jewel, and Design 2 black-and-gold lotus-vine perimeter with two K/spade corner indices. Preserve 5:7 portrait full card. Do not import Design 1's European king, crown, clothing or acanthus.
MAIN CHANGE — FIGURE SCALE AND SURROUND:
The figure is currently too dominant with sparse sprigs on blank ivory. Make his head and torso about 12–15% smaller in linear scale, maintaining natural proportions. Lower the upper cap slightly and lift the inverted lower cap, leaving more decorated room above and around both heads. Keep the joined central robe flowing diagonally, and KEEP BROAD SLEEVES reaching both left and right edges of the interior near the middle of the card, like input 2; the complete figure must not become a small floating isolated bust. Recompose sleeve folds gracefully to span the inner width while the head and torso occupy less area.
Build a generously shaped antique-white reserve around the king, outlined with a narrow beaded gold contour, similar in role to input 2's ivory surround. Outside that reserve and INSIDE the existing narrow outer frame, fill the entire remaining ground with a DENSE BLACK FLORAL FIELD: many intertwining teal lotus leaves, curling gold stems, red-and-ivory lotus blossoms, red buds, little cream blossoms, and small red floral accents closely matching input 3. Rich, continuous, intricate textile ornament at several small scales, not a few widely spaced oversized sprigs. Maintain an elegant quiet ivory halo immediately around face and cap for legibility. Add fine pale-gold cloud and lotus tracery in spare ivory reserve areas as input 2 does, without covering the skin or robe. This should feel as richly finished and densely ornamented as input 2, but wholly Chinese lotus-themed.
SWORD CORRECTION:
Retain one upright straight double-edged Chinese jian on viewer's right, held naturally by a clearly formed hand. Use a slender steel blade with a subtle central ridge, gently tapering edges and a clean pointed tip. Increase the blade-to-hilt ratio so it reads as a one-handed sword instead of a dagger. The blade should appear about 4.5–5 times the usable grip length, fitted inside the card with tip comfortably below the inner top boundary. Remove the current oversized lotus-like butterfly guard. Replace with a compact gilt-bronze guard with a restrained symmetrical Chinese monster-mask relief, informed by the Royal Armouries 15th-century Ming jian. Dark wrapped straight one-hand grip; modest decorated gilt pommel. No broad European crossguard, no fantasy filigree covering the steel, no serrations, katana curve, oversized gem on the guard, or invented writing. Gold embellishment belongs mainly on fittings. This is a historically informed illustrated jian, not a claim to exact artifact reproduction.
TWO-WAY: lower figure, blade, sleeves, floral field, ivory reserve and corner index repeat the upper arrangement under a 180-degree turn; same person and same scale, no independently different lower king. Retain the diagonal join and register the small turquoise center jewel precisely at canvas center. Every botanical detail should visually balance under a half turn.
FINISH: polished painted playing-card illustration, fine warm outlines, softly shaded naturalistic face and hands; rich yellow silk with controlled dragon roundels, luminous antique gold, teal, madder red, ivory and black. Preserve Design 2's OUTER frame design and proportions. Keep K and spade contained in the original upper-left and lower-right index panels; lower marks rotated 180 degrees. No additional labels, text, other cards, scenery, shadows, mockup, watermark, giant center medallion, or new crown. Output one complete revised card image at the source portrait aspect ratio.
sword_correction_prompt:
Edit the supplied Design 2 King of Spades image with ONE strictly localized correction: THE TWO SWORDS ONLY. Preserve all pixels and composition outside the sword blades, guards, grips and pommels as closely as possible: same face, figure scale, robes, hands, beautiful dense floral background, ivory reserve, center jewel, outer frame and indices.
In the upper portrait the sword blade is currently too short, its point begins near 18 percent canvas height. EXTEND THAT SAME STRAIGHT BLADE UPWARD, its tip ending around 10 percent canvas height, safely below the top inner frame. Keep the gripping hand and blade base at the same place. The resulting blade should be about 4.5 times the usable grip length; slim, straight, double edged, tapering gradually to a sharp point, plain steel with a restrained central ridge and clean edge bevels, no engraved filigree. It is a one-handed Chinese JIAN, not a dagger.
REPLACE the conspicuous butterfly/lotus-shaped gold guard completely. Make a smaller, LOW WIDE COMPACT GILT-BRONZE GUARD with shallow downturned shoulders and a small embossed symmetrical Chinese monster-mask face, inspired by a surviving fifteenth-century Ming jian in the Royal Armouries. It must visually read as an ancient Chinese protective mask motif on compact metalwork, NOT an actual creature head, NOT a flower with petals, NOT a large jeweled fantasy guard. Keep its width modest, about twice the blade width. Dark wrapped one-hand grip beneath, modest flattened gilt pommel instead of a dangling jewel.
Apply the exact 180-degree ROTATED version of this sword correction to the lower sword: lower tip extends downward to around 90 percent canvas height. Both hands stay anatomically natural and in place, fingers close correctly around the grips. Sword outline visible against the surrounding ivory and ornament. Preserve the existing 5:7 aspect and polished painted printed-card illustration. No other alterations, no added labels or text, no change to the King, flowers, frame, colors or costume.
